newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary shrs steady before FOMC, MOL up.
newsitem.headline: Hungary shrs steady before FOMC, MOL up.

text.p: The Hungarian share market closed virtually unchanged in calm trade on Tuesday after its highest capitalised issue, oil company MOL, ended steady after releasing its Q1 earnings, traders said.
The BUX index finished at a preliminary 5,887.75 points, up 6.20.
Market participants expect the market to enter a calmer phase amid a slower flow of domestic news, increasing the probability that investors will pay more attention to other markets.

Gabor Sitanyi, analyst at ING Barings in London, said he expected the Polish and Russian share markets to steal the show in the coming months: Poland because of two upcoming share issues worth somewhat above $500 million, and Russia because investors believe it still has the most upside potential.

"Russia is still the number one, the question is whether Poland replaces Hungary in the number two position," Sitanyi said, adding that the Hungarian market starts to be a little more expensive than the Polish market.

On Tuesday the market focused its attention to Magyar Olaj- es Gazipari Rt (MOL)'s shares which finished a shade firmer, at 3,380 forints, up 10, as its first quarter earnings met the market's expectations.
With the second phase of MOL's privatisation over and all Q1 results out, market participants expected foreign investors to be more selective as to which Hungarian shares they buy.
"We're entering a sleepy phase," said Robert Cselovszki of WestLB Investment. "Foreigners are showing interest only in a few shares, such as Zalakeramia, Richter and OTP Bank," he said.
Market participants seem to be mixed on what to expect from the FOMC meeting but ING Barings' Sitanyi said people did not expect too bad a surprise.
"If the FED raises interest rates by at least 0.25 percent, its decision might have some temporary negative impact on bigger, more liquid stocks," Sitanyi said.
As a result the BUX was unlikely to exceed the 6,000 points before the release of first half earnings reports, he added.
On Tuesday tile maker Zalakeramia ended at 7,110 forints, down 180; pharmaceuticals maker Richter at 14,680, up 180 and OTP at 4,275, down 25.
Elsewhere on the market, chemicals TVK finished at 2,680 forints, down 65.
"Selling pressure was quite strong in TVK by one player," said Tamas Revesz of Wintrust. "Its purpose was not to push TVK's price down, but simply the stock had buyers only at lower prices."
